question: How to file an FIR (First Information Report)?
answer: An FIR is the first step to set the criminal law in motion. Under Section 154 CrPC (now Section 173 BNSS), any person can report a cognizable offence at the nearest police station. The police are legally bound to register the FIR — refusal is a punishable offence.

steps.action: Go to the nearest police station
steps.details: Visit the police station having jurisdiction over the area where the offence occurred. You can also file at any police station under the Zero FIR policy.
steps.time_limit: No time limit, but file as early as possible
steps.fees: Free — no fees for FIR registration

steps.action: Narrate the incident to the officer
steps.details: Give a detailed oral or written account of the offence — who, what, when, where. The officer must write it down in the prescribed register.
Under Section 154(2) CrPC, you are entitled to a free copy of the FIR immediately. Do not leave without it.

steps.action: If police refuse to register FIR
steps.details: Send a written complaint to the Superintendent of Police (SP) by registered post. If still no action, approach the Judicial Magistrate under Section 156(3) CrPC to direct the police to register and investigate.

question: How to apply for bail?
answer: Bail is a right in bailable offences and at the discretion of the court in non-bailable offences. You can apply for regular bail, anticipatory bail, or interim bail depending on your situation.

steps.action: Determine the type of bail needed
steps.details: Regular bail (Section 437/439 CrPC) if already arrested. Anticipatory bail (Section 438 CrPC) if you expect arrest. Interim bail for temporary release pending hearing.

steps.action: Engage a lawyer or seek free legal aid
steps.details: Contact a lawyer or approach the District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) for free legal aid under the Legal Services Authorities Act if you cannot afford a lawyer.
Your lawyer files the application before the appropriate court — Magistrate for regular bail in non-bailable offences (Section 437), Sessions Court or High Court for anticipatory bail (Section 438).
steps.fees: Court fees vary by state (typically Rs. 50-500)

steps.details: The court considers: nature of offence, criminal antecedents, flight risk, likelihood of tampering with evidence. Furnish surety and bail bond as directed.

question: What are my rights if I am arrested?
answer: Every arrested person has fundamental rights under the Constitution and the D.K. Basu guidelines laid down by the Supreme Court.

steps.action: Right to know the grounds of arrest
steps.details: The police must inform you why you are being arrested (Article 22(1) of the Constitution).
You can inform a friend, relative, or any person of your choice about your arrest and the place of detention.
You have the right to consult a lawyer of your choice. If you cannot afford one, the state must provide free legal aid.

steps.action: Right to be produced before a Magistrate within 24 hours
steps.details: Under Article 22(2), you must be produced before the nearest Magistrate within 24 hours of arrest (excluding travel time).
Under D.K. Basu guidelines, you must be medically examined every 48 hours during detention.

question: How to register a property sale deed?
answer: All property transactions involving immovable property worth more than Rs. 100 must be registered under the Registration Act, 1908. Unregistered sale deeds are not admissible as evidence.

steps.details: Have a lawyer draft the sale deed with full details: property description, survey number, boundaries, consideration amount, parties' details.
Purchase stamp paper of the requisite value. Stamp duty rates vary by state (typically 5-8% of property value). Pay online or at authorized stamp vendor.
Both buyer and seller (or their power of attorney holders) must appear in person before the Sub-Registrar of the jurisdiction where the property is located. Bring two witnesses.

steps.action: Pay registration fee and biometric verification
steps.details: Pay 1% registration fee. Provide Aadhaar-based biometric verification. The Sub-Registrar will endorse and register the deed.
The registered sale deed will be returned within 15-30 days. Apply for mutation of property records at the local municipal corporation or revenue office.

question: How to file a complaint against a builder for delayed possession under RERA?
answer: Under the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016, homebuyers can file complaints with the state RERA authority for delayed possession, deficient services, or false promises.

steps.action: Check if the project is RERA registered
steps.details: Visit your state RERA website and search by project name or RERA registration number.
Allotment letter, builder-buyer agreement, payment receipts, possession date commitment, any communication about delay.

steps.action: File complaint on state RERA portal
steps.details: Register on your state RERA website, fill the complaint form, upload documents, and pay the prescribed fee (typically Rs. 1,000-5,000).
RERA authority will issue notice to the builder and schedule a hearing. You can appear in person or through a lawyer.
RERA can order: refund with interest, possession with compensation, or penalty on the builder. Appeal lies to RERA Appellate Tribunal within 60 days.

question: How to file for divorce under Hindu Marriage Act?
answer: Either spouse can file for divorce under Section 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. Mutual consent divorce under Section 13B is faster (6-18 months) than contested divorce (2-5 years).

steps.details: Many courts require parties to attempt mediation before proceeding with divorce. Family courts have in-house mediation centres.
File in the Family Court having jurisdiction where the marriage was solemnised, where the couple last lived together, or where the wife currently resides.
steps.fees: Court fees vary by state (typically Rs. 500-2,000)

steps.action: First motion (mutual consent) or contested proceedings
steps.details: In mutual consent: both parties file jointly. Court grants 6-month cooling period (can be waived per SC ruling in Amardeep Singh case). In contested: serve notice on the other party.
Mutual consent: both parties confirm before court after cooling period. Contested: evidence, witnesses, arguments — can take 2-5 years.
Court passes the divorce decree. Effective immediately. Appeal to High Court within 30 days if contested.

question: How to file a domestic violence complaint?
answer: Under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005, any woman who is a victim of physical, emotional, verbal, sexual, or economic abuse can seek protection and relief.

steps.details: Approach the nearest Protection Officer (appointed by the state government) or Women's Cell at a police station. File a DIR in the prescribed form.
The Protection Officer helps you file an application before the Magistrate for protection orders, residence orders, monetary relief, or custody orders.
steps.fees: No court fees (free for DV cases)

steps.details: The Magistrate must hear the case within 3 days of receipt. Can grant ex-parte interim orders on the first hearing itself if there is immediate danger.
steps.time_limit: 3 days for first hearing; 60 days to dispose

question: How to file a consumer complaint?
answer: Under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, any consumer can file a complaint for defective goods, deficient services, unfair trade practices, or overcharging.

steps.action: Send a legal notice to the company
steps.details: Before filing, send a written complaint/legal notice to the company giving them 15-30 days to resolve. Keep proof of delivery.
District Commission: up to Rs. 1 crore. State Commission: Rs. 1-10 crore. National Commission (NCDRC): above Rs. 10 crore.
File online at edaakhil.nic.in or physically at the Consumer Commission. Attach: purchase receipt, warranty card, complaint letters, legal notice, any evidence.
Commission issues notice to the opposite party. Both sides present evidence. Orders typically within 3-5 months for simple cases.

question: How to file a complaint for unpaid wages or wrongful termination?
answer: Workers denied wages or wrongfully terminated can approach the Labour Commissioner, file under the Payment of Wages Act, or raise an industrial dispute under the ID Act.

steps.details: Visit the office of the Assistant Labour Commissioner (Central or State) in your district. File a written complaint with details of employment, wages due, and any termination letter.
The Labour Officer calls both parties for conciliation. If settled, a binding settlement is recorded.

steps.action: If conciliation fails, file in Labour Court
steps.details: File an application before the Labour Court / Industrial Tribunal. Seek reinstatement with back wages (for wrongful termination) or recovery of unpaid wages.

question: How to file a sexual harassment complaint at workplace (POSH)?
answer: Under the POSH Act, 2013, every workplace with 10+ employees must have an Internal Complaints Committee (ICC). Any woman employee can file a written complaint.

steps.details: Submit a written complaint to the Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) within 3 months of the incident (extendable by 3 months in special circumstances).
steps.time_limit: 3 months from incident (+ 3 months extension possible)

steps.details: ICC conducts inquiry following principles of natural justice. Both parties heard. ICC must complete inquiry within 90 days.

steps.action: If no ICC exists, approach Local Complaints Committee
steps.details: For workplaces with fewer than 10 employees or domestic workers, file with the Local Complaints Committee (LCC) at the District Officer.
Sexual harassment may also be a criminal offence under IPC Section 354A. You can simultaneously file an FIR at the police station.

question: How to file an RTI application?
answer: Under the Right to Information Act, 2005, any citizen can request information from any public authority. The authority must respond within 30 days.

steps.details: Every government department has a designated PIO. Find them on the department's website or by calling the office.
Address it to the PIO. Write 'Application under RTI Act, 2005' at the top. Clearly state what information you want. No need to give reasons.
Pay Rs. 10 fee (by postal order, demand draft, or online). BPL families are exempt. Submit by post, in person, or online at rtionline.gov.in.
PIO must respond within 30 days (48 hours if life/liberty is involved). If no response or unsatisfactory response, file first appeal with the First Appellate Authority within 30 days.
steps.time_limit: 30 days response; 30 days for first appeal

steps.details: If first appeal fails, file second appeal with the Central/State Information Commission within 90 days.

question: How to get free legal aid?
answer: Under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987, free legal aid is available to women, children, SC/ST, disabled persons, industrial workers, victims of trafficking, persons in custody, and anyone with annual income below the prescribed limit.

steps.details: Visit the District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) office in your district or the State Legal Services Authority (SLSA). You can also apply online at nalsa.gov.in.
Proof of identity, income certificate (if claiming on income basis), and any documents related to your case.

steps.action: Get a legal aid lawyer assigned
steps.details: DLSA will assign a panel lawyer who will represent you free of charge in all court proceedings.
For basic legal advice without filing a case, call the Tele-Law helpline or visit your nearest Common Service Centre (CSC). A panel lawyer will advise you via video call.

question: How to file a cybercrime complaint?
answer: Cybercrimes can be reported at the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (cybercrime.gov.in) or at your nearest police station. The IT Act, 2000 covers offences like hacking, identity theft, cyber stalking, and online fraud.

steps.details: Register on the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal. File a complaint with screenshots, URLs, transaction IDs, and any other evidence.

steps.action: File an FIR at the nearest police station
steps.details: You can also file an FIR at the local police station or the dedicated Cyber Crime Police Station in your city.
Take screenshots, save emails, note URLs, keep transaction records. Do not delete any messages or communication with the accused.
Call the Cyber Fraud Helpline 1930 immediately for online financial fraud. The earlier you report, the higher the chance of freezing the fraudulent transaction.
steps.time_limit: Report within golden hour for best chance of fund recovery

question: How to file a cheque bounce (Section 138 NI Act) case?
answer: If a cheque issued to you bounces due to insufficient funds, you can file a criminal complaint under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881.

steps.action: Get the cheque return memo from your bank
steps.details: Collect the 'cheque return memo' (dishonour slip) from your bank stating the reason for dishonour (e.g., insufficient funds).

steps.action: Send a legal notice within 30 days
steps.details: Send a written demand notice to the drawer (cheque issuer) via registered post / speed post within 30 days of receiving the return memo. Demand payment of the cheque amount.
The drawer has 15 days from receipt of the notice to make payment. If they pay, matter is settled.

steps.action: File complaint within 30 days of notice expiry
steps.details: If payment is not made within 15 days, file a criminal complaint before the Magistrate having jurisdiction within 30 days of the expiry of the 15-day period.
steps.fees: Court fees as prescribed by state

question: How to file a private criminal complaint before a Magistrate?
answer: If the police refuse to act or the offence is non-cognizable, you can file a private complaint directly before the Judicial Magistrate under Section 200 CrPC (Section 223 BNSS).

steps.details: Write a complaint stating facts of the offence, name and address of the accused, witnesses, and evidence. Include your name, address, and sign it.
Submit the complaint before the Judicial Magistrate First Class (JMFC) having jurisdiction. The Magistrate examines you on oath under Section 200 CrPC.
steps.fees: Court fees as per state rules (Rs. 50-500)

steps.details: The Magistrate may order inquiry under Section 202, direct police investigation under Section 156(3), or take cognizance and issue process (summons/warrant) to the accused.
If cognizance is taken, the accused is summoned. Trial proceeds with examination of complainant's witnesses, cross-examination, and defence evidence.

question: How to get anticipatory bail?
answer: Anticipatory bail under Section 438 CrPC allows a person to seek bail in anticipation of arrest. It must be filed before the Sessions Court or High Court.

steps.details: Anticipatory bail requires legal representation. Contact a lawyer or apply for free legal aid through DLSA.

steps.action: File application before Sessions Court or High Court
steps.details: Application under Section 438 CrPC with an affidavit explaining the facts, fear of arrest, and grounds for bail.
Court may grant interim protection immediately and issue notice to the prosecution. Full hearing follows where court considers nature of offence, applicant's antecedents, and likelihood of fleeing.
If granted, court imposes conditions — surrender passport, mark attendance at police station, not leave jurisdiction without permission. Breach leads to cancellation.

question: How to file a complaint for online harassment or cyber stalking?
answer: Online harassment and cyber stalking are punishable under the IT Act and IPC/BNS. You can report at cybercrime.gov.in and also file an FIR.

steps.details: Take screenshots of harassing messages, emails, social media posts. Note usernames, URLs, timestamps. Do not delete anything.
File a complaint on the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal with all evidence attached.
Visit the nearest police station or Cyber Crime Police Station. File FIR under Section 354D IPC (stalking), Section 509 IPC (word/gesture to insult modesty), and Section 67 IT Act.
If the harassment is severe, apply to the Magistrate for a protection order. You can also seek removal of content by reporting to the social media platform.

question: How to evict a tenant who refuses to vacate?
answer: Eviction proceedings depend on whether the tenancy is governed by state Rent Control Act or the Transfer of Property Act. The landlord must follow due process — self-help eviction is illegal.

steps.action: Serve a legal notice to vacate
steps.details: Send a notice under Section 106 TPA giving the tenant 15 days (monthly tenancy) or 6 months (yearly tenancy) to vacate. Send by registered post with AD.
steps.time_limit: 15 days to 6 months depending on tenancy type

steps.details: If tenant doesn't vacate after notice period, file an eviction petition before the Rent Controller (if Rent Control Act applies) or a civil suit before the Civil Court.
steps.fees: Court fees based on annual rent

steps.details: Court issues summons to tenant. Both parties present evidence. Grounds for eviction: non-payment of rent, subletting, damage to property, personal need of landlord, etc.
If court orders eviction, and tenant still refuses, apply for execution of decree. Court bailiff will enforce the eviction order.

question: How to file a mutation application for inherited property?
answer: After inheriting property (through will or succession), you need to get the revenue records updated in your name through a mutation application at the local tehsil/municipal office.

steps.details: Death certificate of the deceased, succession certificate / probate / legal heir certificate, original property documents, identity proof of all legal heirs, no objection from other heirs (if applicable).
Submit mutation application at the Tehsildar's office (rural) or Municipal Corporation (urban) along with documents and prescribed fee.
Revenue officer verifies documents, publishes notice for objections (15-30 days), conducts spot inspection if needed, and holds hearing.
If no valid objection, revenue records are updated in your name. Collect the mutated extract (khata/patta/7/12 extract depending on state).

question: How to apply for a succession certificate?
answer: A succession certificate under the Indian Succession Act, 1925 is required to establish the legal right of an heir to the debts and securities of a deceased person.

steps.details: File a petition under Section 372 of the Indian Succession Act before the District Court having jurisdiction where the deceased ordinarily resided.
steps.fees: Court fees based on value of estate (varies by state)

steps.details: Court publishes notice in newspaper giving 45 days for objections from any person.
If no objection, court grants succession certificate specifying debts and securities the heir is entitled to collect.
Present the succession certificate to banks, mutual fund houses, insurance companies, etc. to claim the deceased's assets.

question: How to claim maintenance under Section 125 CrPC?
answer: Section 125 CrPC provides for maintenance to wives, children, and parents who are unable to maintain themselves. It is a quick remedy available in the Magistrate's court.

steps.details: File before the Magistrate of the area where the applicant resides or where the respondent resides or works. No court fee in most states.
Magistrate issues notice to the respondent (husband/father/son) to appear and show cause why maintenance should not be ordered.
Court can order interim maintenance pending final hearing if the applicant's need is established prima facie.
After hearing both sides, Magistrate fixes monthly maintenance amount based on respondent's income, applicant's needs, and standard of living. Non-payment can lead to arrest.
steps.time_limit: Should be decided within 60 days (as per amendment)

question: How to get a child custody order?
answer: Child custody disputes are decided by the Family Court based on the welfare of the child as the paramount consideration, not the rights of the parents.

steps.action: File custody petition in Family Court
steps.details: File under Section 26 of HMA (for Hindus) or the Guardians and Wards Act, 1890 (for all). The court where the child ordinarily resides has jurisdiction.
Court can grant interim custody to one parent and visitation rights to the other while the case is pending.
Court may appoint a counsellor to assess the child's living conditions with each parent and submit a welfare report.
Court decides based on: child's age and wishes (if old enough), emotional and educational needs, capacity of each parent, any history of abuse. Mother usually preferred for children under 5.

question: How to obtain a legal heir certificate?
answer: A legal heir certificate establishes who the legal heirs of a deceased person are. It is issued by the Tehsildar (revenue authority) and is needed for claiming pension, insurance, bank deposits, etc.

steps.details: Submit application with: death certificate, Aadhaar of deceased and all legal heirs, ration card, self-declaration listing all legal heirs.
Revenue officer may conduct local enquiry and publish notice for objections (7-15 days).
If no objection, Tehsildar issues legal heir certificate listing all legal heirs and their relationship to the deceased.

question: How to claim insurance and what to do if claim is rejected?
answer: If your insurance claim is rejected or delayed unreasonably, you can approach the Insurance Ombudsman or file a consumer complaint.

steps.action: File claim with the insurance company
steps.details: Submit all required documents (claim form, medical records/bills, FIR for accident/theft, death certificate for life insurance) within the policy's notification period.
steps.time_limit: As per policy (usually 30-90 days for intimation)

steps.action: If rejected, send written complaint to insurer
steps.details: Write to the Grievance Redressal Officer of the insurance company. They must respond within 15 days.
If unsatisfied, file complaint with the Insurance Ombudsman (claims up to Rs. 30 lakh for life, Rs. 20 lakh for general). Free of charge. Decision is binding on insurer.
Alternatively, file a complaint before the Consumer Commission for deficiency in service. Can claim compensation beyond just the claim amount.

question: How to file a complaint for medical negligence?
answer: Medical negligence by a hospital or doctor can be complained about to the medical council, consumer forum, or through a criminal complaint.

steps.details: Under Section 1.3 of Indian Medical Council Regulations, you have the right to your complete medical records. Request copies of all prescriptions, reports, discharge summary, operation notes.
Consult another doctor to get an independent opinion on whether there was negligence or deviation from standard medical practice.

steps.action: File complaint with State Medical Council
steps.details: Lodge complaint with the State Medical Council against the doctor. Council can suspend or revoke their licence.
File before the Consumer Commission for compensation (medical services are 'services' under CPA 2019). Attach expert opinion, medical records, and bills.
If patient died due to negligence, file FIR under Section 304A IPC (death by negligence) or Section 338 IPC (grievous hurt by negligence).

question: How to get a refund for a defective product bought online?
answer: E-commerce purchases are covered under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 and the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020. You can claim refund, replacement, or compensation.

steps.details: Use the e-commerce platform's return/refund mechanism within the return window. Document the defect with photos/videos.
Under E-Commerce Rules, every platform must have a grievance officer who must acknowledge within 48 hours and resolve within 1 month.
Call 1915 or file at consumerhelpline.gov.in. They mediate with the company for resolution.
If unresolved, file at edaakhil.nic.in against both the seller and the e-commerce platform (they are jointly liable under CPA 2019).

question: How to claim EPF (Provident Fund) withdrawal?
answer: Employees can withdraw PF after leaving a job. Full withdrawal is allowed after 2 months of unemployment or at retirement (58 years). Partial withdrawal is allowed for specific purposes.

steps.action: Check your UAN and link Aadhaar
steps.details: Log in to unifiedportal-mem.epfindia.gov.in. Ensure your UAN (Universal Account Number) is active and Aadhaar, PAN, and bank account are linked and verified.
Go to Online Services > Claim (Form 19 for full withdrawal, Form 31 for partial). Select claim type, enter bank details, and submit.
If filing through employer, the claim needs employer's digital attestation. If UAN-Aadhaar linked, you can file directly without employer.
Track status on the EPFO portal. Processing takes 10-20 days. Amount credited directly to linked bank account.

question: How to claim maternity benefit?
answer: Under the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961 (and Code on Social Security, 2020), women employees are entitled to 26 weeks of paid maternity leave for the first two children.

steps.details: Inform your employer about the expected delivery date and your intention to take maternity leave. Provide medical certificate.
steps.time_limit: Notify at least 8 weeks before expected delivery

steps.details: Employer must grant 26 weeks of leave (8 weeks before delivery + 18 weeks after) at average daily wage. Cannot be denied or terminated during this period.
File complaint with the Inspector appointed under the Maternity Benefit Act. Inspector can order the employer to pay.
If covered under ESI scheme, claim maternity benefit through ESI by submitting Form 19 at the local ESI office.

question: How to file a PIL (Public Interest Litigation)?
answer: A PIL can be filed directly before the Supreme Court (Article 32) or High Court (Article 226) for enforcement of fundamental rights or public interest issues.

steps.details: PIL must concern a matter of public interest — not a private grievance. Environmental damage, violation of fundamental rights of a group, government inaction on public health, etc.
Include: facts of the public interest issue, fundamental rights violated, prayer/relief sought, supporting documents. A letter to the Chief Justice can also be treated as PIL.

steps.action: File before High Court or Supreme Court
steps.details: File before the High Court of the state (Article 226) or directly before the Supreme Court (Article 32) if fundamental rights are involved. Court fees are nominal for PILs.
Court examines whether the petition raises genuine public interest. If admitted, court issues notice to respondents (usually government bodies) and monitors compliance with orders.

question: How to file a complaint with the Lokpal / Lokayukta?
answer: Complaints about corruption by public servants can be filed with the Lokpal (central) or Lokayukta (state) under the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013.

steps.details: Write a complaint with: name of the public servant, their designation, nature of corruption/misconduct, supporting evidence (documents, recordings, etc.).
File at lokpal.gov.in for central officials, or the state Lokayukta website for state officials. Can also send by registered post.
Lokpal conducts preliminary inquiry within 60 days. If prima facie case exists, orders investigation by CBI or other agency.
Investigation must be completed within 6 months (extendable by 6 months). Special court trials corruption cases.

question: How to file a human rights complaint with NHRC?
answer: The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) investigates complaints of human rights violations by public servants. File within one year of the violation.

steps.action: File complaint online or by post
steps.details: File at hrcnet.nic.in or send by post to NHRC, Manav Adhikar Bhawan, Block-C, GPO Complex, New Delhi - 110023. Include detailed facts, names of violators, evidence.
NHRC examines the complaint. May call for report from government authority, conduct investigation through its own team, or direct state authority to investigate.
NHRC can recommend compensation to the victim, prosecution of the violator, or policy changes. While not binding, government must respond within one month.

question: How to file for insolvency under IBC?
answer: Under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, creditors can initiate insolvency proceedings against a defaulting company before the NCLT if the default is Rs. 1 crore or more.

steps.details: Financial creditor files under Section 7, operational creditor under Section 9. Include proof of default, demand notice (for operational creditors), and proposed insolvency resolution professional.
NCLT must admit or reject within 14 days. If admitted, moratorium is imposed — no suits, no recovery, no transfer of assets.
IRP/RP takes over management. Committee of Creditors formed. Resolution plan invited. CIRP must complete within 330 days.
If resolution plan approved by 66% of CoC and NCLT, company continues under new management. If no plan, company goes into liquidation.

question: How to register a trademark?
answer: Trademark registration protects your brand name, logo, or slogan. Register online at ipindiaonline.gov.in. Registration gives you exclusive right to use the mark for 10 years (renewable).

steps.details: Search the Trade Marks Registry at ipindiaonline.gov.in to check if your desired mark is already registered or applied for.
File Form TM-A at ipindiaonline.gov.in. Choose the right class (Nice Classification). Individual applicants get 50% fee concession.
Examiner reviews the application. May raise objections (similar existing marks, descriptive marks). You must respond within 30 days. Hearing if needed.
If accepted, mark is published in Trade Marks Journal for 4 months. Anyone can oppose during this period.
If no opposition (or opposition fails), registration certificate is issued. Valid for 10 years from filing date, renewable.

question: How to file a complaint with the National Green Tribunal?
answer: The NGT hears cases related to environmental protection, forest conservation, and pollution. Any person can file within 6 months of the cause of action (extendable by 60 days).

steps.details: Illegal construction in eco-sensitive zone, industrial pollution, illegal tree felling, groundwater contamination, noise pollution, etc.
File at the NGT bench having jurisdiction (principal bench in Delhi, circuit benches in Bhopal, Pune, Kolkata, Chennai). No lawyer mandatory — you can appear in person.
steps.time_limit: Within 6 months of cause of action

steps.details: NGT issues notice to polluter/violator. Can order interim relief (stop construction, close factory). Final order with compensation.

question: How to file a pollution complaint against a factory or construction site?
answer: Pollution complaints can be filed with the State Pollution Control Board (SPCB), local municipal corporation, or the NGT.

steps.details: Take photos/videos of the pollution source. Note the type (air, water, noise, solid waste), location, time, and impact on the area.
File complaint online at the state PCB website or at cpcb.nic.in. Include evidence and location details.
For construction noise, garbage burning, or local nuisance, file complaint with the municipal corporation. They can issue closure/stop-work notice.

steps.action: File at NGT if no action
steps.details: If SPCB/municipal corporation takes no action within 30 days, file application before the National Green Tribunal.

question: How to file a motor accident claim?
answer: Victims of road accidents (or their families) can claim compensation from the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (MACT) under the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

steps.action: File FIR and get accident report
steps.details: Ensure FIR is filed at the nearest police station. Obtain a copy of the FIR and the Motor Vehicle Accident Report.
Collect all medical bills, treatment records, disability certificate (if permanent disability), and death certificate (if fatal accident).
File before the MACT having jurisdiction (where the accident occurred or where the claimant resides). Claim against the vehicle owner, driver, and insurance company.
steps.fees: No court fee for accident victims

steps.details: MACT assesses compensation based on: age, income, nature of injury/death, dependents. Award includes medical expenses + loss of income + pain and suffering. Insurance company pays.

question: How to apply for a passport and what to do if it is delayed or rejected?
answer: Passport applications are filed online at passportindia.gov.in. If delayed beyond 30 days (normal) or 7 days (tatkal), you can file grievances or approach the court.

steps.details: Fill the application form on passportindia.gov.in, pay fee online, and book an appointment at the nearest Passport Seva Kendra (PSK).
Bring original documents (Aadhaar, PAN, address proof, old passport if renewal). Biometrics are captured at the PSK.
Police conduct address verification. If clear, passport dispatched within 7-30 days.

steps.action: If delayed or rejected, file grievance
steps.details: File grievance on passportindia.gov.in. If still unresolved, approach the Regional Passport Officer. As last resort, file writ petition before the High Court under Article 226.
